answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring new identities to be vouched for by established agents who stake their own reputation. A voucher's standing falls if its vouchee commits fraud, so sponsors check newcomers carefully. Each identity must also complete a slow, verifiable onboarding task before transacting at full speed, making mass creation costly in time and attention. Like a lantern passed hand to hand, trust spreads only through accountable links; a sparrow cannot pretend to be a flock, and a raven that vouches for fakes soon loses its own standing.
